# 3 Maccabees Chapter 1 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Greek MS (Codex Alexandrinus) | **Section:** Ptolemy at Raphia and Jerusalem

---

**1:1** When Philopator learned from those who returned that the regions he had controlled had been seized by Antiochus, he gave orders to all his forces, both infantry and cavalry, took with him his sister Arsinoe, and marched out to the regions near Raphia, where Antiochus and his forces were encamped.

**1:2** But one Theodotus, intending to carry out his treachery, took with him the finest of the arms that had previously been assigned to him, and crossed over by night to Ptolemy's tent to kill him single-handedly, and thus to end the war.

**1:3** But Dositheus, known as the son of Drimylus, a Jew by birth who had later changed his religion and abandoned the ancestral customs, had the king removed and arranged for a certain worthless man to sleep in the tent in his place; and it turned out that Theodotus killed this man instead.

**1:4** After a fierce battle had taken place, and affairs were looking rather favorably for Philopator, Antiochus saw that the situation was serious and that his forces were being overwhelmed.

**1:5** But Antiochus saw that his allies were giving way and that Ptolemy's forces were pressing forward. He retreated to a position where he could regroup.

**1:6** After the battle Ptolemy made a display of his valor and visited the various cities, encouraging the inhabitants and inspiring confidence.

**1:7** Having thus confirmed the courage of his followers, he proceeded to Judea, and came to Jerusalem and offered sacrifice as was fitting to the greatest God.

**1:8** He made thank offerings, and did what was appropriate for the holy place, and upon entering the precinct and being struck with admiration at its orderliness and beauty,

**1:9** he marveled at the good order of the temple and decided that he wished to enter the inner sanctuary.

**1:10** But when they told him that it was not permitted for anyone to enter, not even any of the priests, but only for the high priest who presides over all, and he alone only once a year, Ptolemy was not persuaded.

**1:11** Even when the law was read to him, he did not cease from insisting that he would enter, saying: Even if they are refused this permission, it should not be so with me.

**1:12** And he asked why, when he had entered all other temples, none of the priests in those places had prevented him.

**1:13** Someone answered in an absurd manner that he was wrong to boast of this.

**1:14** But since he was about to proceed into the sanctuary regardless, the priests together with all the people fell down and begged him to turn aside from his impious determination.

**1:15** A great tumult arose in the city, and the priests in their vestments threw themselves down before the altar and cried out to heaven with earnest prayers for help in this critical situation.

**1:16** Their cry was heard, and the city resounded with weeping and lamentation.

**1:17** Those who were in their houses rushed to the scene, and all abandoned whatever was in their hands and crowded to the spectacle of the most pitiable supplication.

**1:18** The women had locked themselves in with their children and had shut the doors; some leaned out from the windows, others from the roofs, and stretched their hands toward heaven and made the most pitiful supplications.

**1:19** It was pathetic to see the prostration of the whole multitude, and the outpouring of expectation of the high priest in his great agony.

**1:20** While they were thus pleading and supplicating, calling to the Almighty Lord to help them in this time of crisis, one of their number, the high priest Shimon, stretched himself out before the sanctuary and prayed in this manner.

**1:21** O Lord, Lord, King of the heavens and Master of all creation, Holy One among the holy ones, Sole Ruler, Almighty, give ear to us who are burdened with distress by a wicked and impure man who is puffed up with audacity and power.

**1:22** For you, the Creator of all things and Governor of the whole world, are a righteous Ruler, and you judge those who act with violence and arrogance.

**1:23** You destroyed those of old who committed unrighteous deeds among whom were also the giants who had confidence in their strength and boldness, on whom you inflicted destruction without measure.

**1:24** You made the Sodomites who acted lawlessly known to all, having made them an example to those who should come after.

**1:25** You made known your power to the presumptuous Pharaoh who had enslaved your holy people Israel, afflicting them with various and severe punishments.

**1:26** And when he pursued them with chariots and a great multitude, you overwhelmed him in the depths of the sea, but carried safely through those who had put their trust in you, the Ruler over the whole of creation.

**1:27** And when they had seen your mighty hand, they praised you, the Almighty.

**1:28** You, O King, when you created the boundless and immeasurable earth, chose this city and sanctified this place for the glory of your name, even though you need nothing; and when you had glorified it by your magnificent manifestation, you made it a firm foundation for the glory of your great and honored name.

**1:29** And loving the house of Israel, you promised that if we should fall away and trouble should befall us, and we came to this place and prayed, you would hear our prayer.

**1:30** And indeed you are faithful and true.
